competition: Chile International Mathematical Olympiad and Iberoamerican Olympiad Team Selection Tests

problems.problem: Prove that the equation $$x^x+y^y=z^z$$ has no solutions in integers.
Let $a$ be a natural number such that $a+n^2$ can be written as a sum of two squares for every natural number $n$. Prove that $a$ is the square of a natural number.

The incircle of triangle $ABC$ touches $AC$ and $BC$ at $E$ and $D$, respectively. The excircle opposite $A$ touches lines $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$ at $A_1$, $B_1$ and $C_1$, respectively. Let $L=DE\cap A_1B_1$. Prove that $L$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $A_1BC_1$.
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f(x+1)=\frac12+\sqrt{f(x)-f(x)^2}$$ for every real $x$. Prove that there is a real number $b>0$ such that $f(x+b)=f(x)$ for every real $x$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $P,Q,R$ lie on sides $AB,BC,CA$, respectively, such that $$\frac{AP}{AB}=\frac{BQ}{BC}=\frac{CR}{CA}=\frac1n,$$ where $n$ is a positive integer. Segments $AQ$ and $CP$ meet at $D$, segments $BR$ and $AQ$ meet at $E$, and segments $BR$ and $CP$ meet at $F$. Calculate $$\frac{\operatorname{Area}(ABC)}{\operatorname{Area}(DEF)}.$$
Let $x_0=5$ and $x_{n+1}=x_n+\frac1{x_n}$ for $n\ge0$. Prove that $$45<x_{1000}<45.1.$$
Determine the number of pairs of functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, $$f(g(n))=n+2015,\qquad g(f(n))=n^2+2015.$$

In the country of Muilejistan, a network of roads connects all its cities. Between any two cities there is exactly one route without backtracking, that is, one route in which a traveller never returns along the road just travelled. The longest possible route between two cities has length $600$ kilometres. For example, the route from Mlar to Nlar is $600$ kilometres long, and the route from Klar to Glar is also $600$ kilometres long. (a) Jalim leaves Mlar for Nlar at noon, and Kalim leaves Klar for Glar at noon. If they travel at the same speed, prove that they meet somewhere along their routes. (b) If the distance in kilometres between each pair of cities is an integer, prove that the distance in kilometres from Glar to Mlar is even.
Prove that the orthocentre, incentre and circumcentre of an acute scalene triangle are not collinear.
Let $x,y>0$ be real numbers. Prove that $$\left(1+\frac1x\right)\left(1+\frac1y\right)\ge\left(1+\frac2{x+y}\right)^2.$$

An equilateral triangle of side length $20$ is subdivided by lines parallel to its sides into $20^2=400$ equilateral triangles of side length $1$. Some unit segments that are sides of these small triangles are to be coloured red, so that no small triangle has all three sides red. Determine the largest possible number of unit segments that can be coloured red.

There are $2016$ points near a line such that the distance from each point to the line is less than $1$ centimetre, and the distance between any two points is greater than $2$ centimetres. Prove that two of the points are at distance at least $17$ metres.

A set $A$ of integers is called admissible if, whenever $x,y\in A$, we have $$x^2+kxy+y^2\in A$$ for every integer $k$. Determine all pairs of nonzero integers $m,n$ for which the only admissible set containing both $m$ and $n$ is the set of all integers.

Let $f,g$ be nonzero polynomials with integer coefficients and $\deg f>\deg g$. Suppose that the polynomial $pf+g$ has a rational root for infinitely many primes $p$. Prove that $f$ has a rational root. A rational root of a polynomial $f$ is a number $q\in\mathbb Q$ such that $f(q)=0$.

The sets of rational numbers $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_5\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_5\}$ both contain $0$ and satisfy $$\{a_i+b_j:1\le i,j\le5\}=\{0,1,2,\ldots,24\}.$$ Determine these sets. The set on the left consists of all possible sums of an element of $A$ and an element of $B$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB\ne AC$. Let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$, and $E$ the intersection of the bisector of $\angle BAC$ with $BC$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the second intersections of the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ with $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Prove that lines $AD,BP,CQ$ are concurrent.

Let $n$ be a natural number with more than $2021$ decimal digits, none of which is $8$ or $9$. Suppose that $n$ is relatively prime to $2021$. Prove that one digit of $n$ can be increased by at most $2$ so that the resulting number is divisible by $2021$.

Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be the circumcircles of triangles $ABC$ and $ABM$, respectively. Determine the ratio of the areas enclosed by $C_1$ and $C_2$.

Determine the number of pairs of positive integers $(p,k)$ such that $p$ is prime and $p^2+2^k$ is a perfect square less than $2023$. A perfect square is the square of an integer.
Solve the following system in real numbers: $$\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac xy+\frac yz+\frac zx=\frac xz+\frac zy+\frac yx,\\x^2+y^2+z^2=294,\\x+y+z=0.\end{cases}$$

On a $10\times10$ chessboard there are $91$ white pawns on distinct squares. Nico takes a white pawn, paints it black and places it on an empty square, repeating this process until all the pawns are black. Prove that at some stage there are two pawns of different colours on squares sharing a side.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $D$ and $E$ be the feet of the altitudes from $B$ and $C$, respectively. Let $E^{\prime}$ be the reflection of $E$ across line $BD$, and suppose that $E^{\prime}$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Let $C^{\prime}$ be the reflection of $C$ across line $BD$. Prove that triangle $C^{\prime}AE$ is isosceles, and determine the ratio $AD:DC$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/cl_imo_2023_p5_fig.png
For $n=0,1,2,\ldots$, consider the sequence $$a_n=4^n c+\frac{4^n-(-1)^n}{5}.$$ Determine the values of $c$ for which the sequence contains a perfect square.

A function $f$ on the nonnegative integers satisfies: (i) $f(n)$ is an integer for every $n$; (ii) $f(0)=1$; (iii) $$f(n+1)>f(n)+f(n-1)+\cdots+f(0)$$ for every $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. Determine the smallest possible value of $f(2023)$.

Determine the smallest positive integer $n$ with the following property: for every triple of positive integers $x,y,z$ such that $x\mid y^3$, $y\mid z^3$ and $z\mid x^3$, we also have $$xyz\mid(x+y+z)^n.$$

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB<AC$, and let $\omega$ be its circumcircle. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and $N$ the midpoint of the arc $BC$ of $\omega$ containing $A$. The circumcircle of triangle $AMN$ meets sides $AB$ and $AC$ again at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Prove that $BP=CQ$.
Let $a,b,c>0$ satisfy $a+b+c\le\frac32$. Find the minimum of $$a+b+c+\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c.$$
Let $m\ge2$ and $k\ge1$ be integers. Prove that $$(m-1)^2\mid m^k-1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad m-1\mid k.$$

In triangle $ABC$, let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$. Let $P$ lie on segment $CD$. Let $Q$ be the intersection of lines $AP$ and $CB$, and $R$ the intersection of lines $BP$ and $CA$. Prove that $\angle RDC=\angle QDC$.
Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. Prove that if none of $f(-1),f(0),f(1)$ is divisible by $3$, then $f(m)\ne0$ for every integer $m$.

A collection of regular polygons with equal side lengths is said to fit if, when the polygons are placed around a common vertex, they exactly fill a neighbourhood of that point in the plane. For example, a square fits with two regular octagons. Determine all possible collections of regular polygons that fit.

Find all positive integers $n$ for which an $n\times n$ square can be tiled using only tetrominoes of the shape shown in the figure.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/cl_ibero_2024_p3_fig.png
Prove that for positive real numbers $a,b,c$, $$\frac{a+3c}{a+b}+\frac{c+3a}{b+c}+\frac{4b}{c+a}\ge6.$$

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $P$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and $K$ the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$. Let $D$ lie on segment $AP$ such that $\angle BDC=90^\circ$. Let $E$ be the second intersection of line $BC$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ADK$. Let $F$ be the second intersection of line $AE$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Prove that $\angle AFD=90^\circ$.
At a gathering there are $N$ people, no two of whom know each other. Prove that they can be introduced to one another in such a way that no three people have the same number of acquaintances.
Let $a,b,c,d$ be real numbers satisfying $abcd=1$ and $$a+\frac1a+b+\frac1b+c+\frac1c+d+\frac1d=0.$$ Prove that at least one of $ab,ac,ad$ equals $-1$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB<AC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$, and $D$ the point on segment $AC$ such that $DB=DC$. Let $E$ be the intersection other than $B$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABM$ with line $BD$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the intersections of line $BC$ with lines $EM$ and $AE$, respectively. Prove that $P$ is the midpoint of $BQ$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/cl_imo_2025_p4_fig.png

Let $u_n$ be the $n$th Fibonacci number, with $u_1=u_2=1$ and $u_{n+1}=u_n+u_{n-1}$ for $n\ge2$. For each prime $p$, let $n(p)$ be the smallest positive integer $n$ for which $p\mid u_n$. Find the smallest possible value of $p-n(p)$.
How many nondecreasing surjective functions $f:A\to B$ are there, where $$A=\{1,2,\ldots,100\},\qquad B=\{1,2,\ldots,50\}?$$
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be distinct positive integers, none of whose decimal expansions contains two consecutive digits equal to $9$. Prove that $$\frac1{a_1}+\cdots+\frac1{a_n}\le2025.$$
Determine all functions $f:\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R$ such that $$f(x)+f\left(\frac1{1-x}\right)=x$$ for every $x\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\}$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral whose four side lengths are all distinct. Choose a point $P$ inside $ABCD$ such that $$\angle APB=\frac{\angle C+\angle D}{2},\qquad\angle CPD=\frac{\angle A+\angle B}{2},$$ where $\angle A,\angle B,\angle C,\angle D$ are the interior angles of the quadrilateral. Prove that the distances from $P$ to lines $AB$ and $CD$ are equal.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with an obtuse angle at $A$ and incentre $I$. The circles through $A,B,I$ and through $A,C,I$ meet line $BC$ again at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Lines $AX$ and $BI$ meet at $P$, and lines $AY$ and $CI$ meet at $Q$. Prove that quadrilateral $BCQP$ is cyclic.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $$2xyf(x^2-y^2)=(x^2-y^2)f(x)f(2y)$$ for all real numbers $x,y$.
Let $a,b$ be positive integers such that $a+b^3$ is divisible by $a^2+3ab+3b^2-1$. Prove that $a^2+3ab+3b^2-1$ is divisible by the cube of an integer greater than $1$.

Let $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_{2026})$ be a sequence of positive integers, not necessarily distinct. Let $m$ be the number of triples $(i,j,k)$ with $1\le i<j<k\le2026$ such that $$a_i+1=a_j=a_k-1.$$ Find the largest possible value of $m$ over all such sequences $A$.
